transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 6 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 4 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 0 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 4 votes

[The 6 of you who have voted that women are at the fourth step, you mean that young women have power and freedom to make many major life decisions. The four of you who have voted for the third step you imply that young women have power and freedom to make some major life decisions.]
At the age we are we have to express our feelings and take actions over them.
[Another one?] In doing business for example you need to decide on what to sell and which goods not sell depending on the capital you have.
[Why do you think you are not at the fifth step?] As much as we make decisions, we are still listening to our parents and guardians for a final decision.

[Why do you think some of you are still at the third level in as far as the freedom and power to make decision is concerned?] we still depend on parents for most of the decision. I have to wait for my parents to give out the timetable for working. I cannot go working without parents directing me to go and do a certain activity.
[At what step would you rate yourselves during the past ten years?] (All respondents voted for the first step)

[As you have all voted for the first step, you imply that young women almost had no power or freedom to make decisions] The minds of young women are at least opened up now compared to the past ten years. Yes, I was young, but I think women were still backward by then. I could see my mother always at home.
My mother would not even do any kind of business and she had not gone to school. Nowadays young women are in c=schools, for example and they are good with business
I think going to school is important. People who have gone to school are able to know their directions in life. They determine who they want to become in the future.
[Another one?] In school we get to know what is bad and differentiate it from good.
By going to school we get to know our rights and the geography of the world.
[Another one?] In school also we are able to know how to read and write because many people who never go to school never get a chance to know about this in their life.
[Until what grade do boys generally study in this community?] Form four is common for boys and girls, normally. But girls can drop in between because of pregnancy.
[How many of you think that boys in this community study up to form four?] All respondents raised their hands.
[And what about girls?] Form four.
[How many of you think that girls in this community study up to form four?] All respondents raise their hands.
[Is getting pregnant during secondary school common?] Yes it is common. Many get pregnant. But they can return to school if they wish
Form four.
[Why:] That is what is suggested by government.
[Another one?] Form Six.
[Why?] Then you can go even to university.
[How many of you think boys should study to form six?] (All respondents raised their hands)
[Why?] By this level the boys have reached a stage when they can analyze life issues very few boys analyze issues before this level.
[Why do you think boys never analyze issues before this level?] It is like they are still behaving in childish way. They are not yet mature.
We girls are faster in understanding life challenges and techniques to win in life.
But I think that girls should at least go as far as form six
[Why?] This is because they can get married at an age which is slightly higher than when they finish form four; by then, they are mature.

[Now, can’t boys get married at an early age if they stop schooling at Form Four level?] Very few boys do that when compared to the girls who get married after Form four. Boys will still be very childish (laughter)
All respondents: Yes.

[Why do you think parents show commitment to educating both daughters and sons?] During the past parents used to educate boys alone saying that girls will get married and will not benefit their families and that they will be cared for by their husbands.
[What has changed now?] I think now the government has given priorities to girls in education and encouraged the parents to abandon old traditions.
The farming in maize and rice; this is for food.
[What else do girls in this community learn about when they are young in this village?] We also learn how to manage men.

[How?] You see, men can ruin your life. So, we are taught how to avoid them. For example, not to move at night; not to drink; not to talk to men you do not know; not to receive money from men; and so many other things.
Some of us, but very few, have been taught how to grow various vegetables, even though the most common learnt farming activities regard maize and rice.

Reasons for ending education
• Early sex that lead to early pregnancies
• Some do decide on their own to end studying convincing themselves that they are not intelligent.
• Indiscipline to teachers, students and parents
• Economic difficulties.
• Being deceived by outside men that they will marry them and lead them to a better life.
• Health problems.

Two most important reasons
• Early sex that lead to early pregnancies
• Indiscipline to teachers, students and parents
[Which are the two most important reasons that make girls in this community to end education?] - Early sex that lead to early pregnancies
- Indiscipline to teachers, students and parents
All respondents: Yes.
[What were your special goals for the future?] Becoming a tailor.
[Another one?] Becoming a teacher.
[Another one?] Becoming a Doctor.
[Another one?] Becoming a businesswoman.

[What happened? Are you still pursuing your goals?] Becoming a tailor is something I am still trying to pursue. I am already going for training, even though my teacher is harassing me. I work with her and she does not pay me at all. She only gives me work and she says that is how I have to learn.

For me, becoming a teacher is still a big dream. I do not see how I can go there, with my little marks at school and the rising school fees everywhere. I am not sure if I shall ever become a teacher, even if that is what I really wanted and want!

[Penye nia pana njia (where there is intention, there is a way). Another one?] I am like my friend. I am not sure if I shall make it with becoming a doctor. No money, no good teachers at school no encouragement, no everything.
For me, becoming a businesswoman is a must. I am already doing something. So, I am on the right truck.
Farming and petty business. What else can they do?
[Another one?] Some move to towns to find jobs. If they were like teachers, they can always find work with the private business schools or wok with NGOs
[What else do women do when they are no longer students?] They also can become laborers in farms.
[What are the two commonly done activities by the young girls in this community once they are no longer students?] Farming and working for money.
[Do we all agree to this?] All respondents: Yes.
They should continue with studying if possible.
[How?] If for example after standard seven or Form four there is an opportunity to join high level studies or vocational training, they should go as far as there.
[Another one?] They should do the farming because they can have food and they can earn income when they sell something. They should not be dependent on their parents or relatives
I think that they need to be given capital in order to start doing business. We should be independent financially and we should also be very busy.
Nowadays you see that there is insecurity everywhere. I propose that we should also join the military (laughter).

New agricultural or NRM practices
• The use of tractors in farming
• The introduction of new maize variety of Star
• Farming by water pumps machines in vegetable growing.
• Fertilizer and manure application for example Minjingo and UREA

Most important for the women of the community (top 2)
• Farming by water pumps machines in vegetable growing (irrigation).
• The use of tractors in farming.

Most important for the men of the community (top 2)
• Farming by water pumps machines in vegetable growing (irrigation).
• The use of tractors in farming.
- Farming by irrigation using water pump machines in vegetable growing.
- The use of tractors in farming.

[Why important?] They have been adopted mostly by many people who are seriously farming. During the past years, people used hand hoes and human laborers. Today, however, people are trying hard to adopt tractor usage.

[Why is the usage of water pumps machines in vegetable growing so important to people like you in this community?] This is important to the whole community because the men do grow and sell the vegetable to women who go selling in the village and town markets as well.
[And which have been most important agricultural practices for the boys of your age in this community?] -Farming by irrigation using water pumps machines in vegetable growing.
-The use of tractors in farming.

[Why do you think farming by irrigation has been the most important agricultural practice to the young men and boys of your age in this community?] Young men are involved in vegetable growing that earns them income.
[Another one?] These are the new practices that are being introduced to be adopted by the young men and women in our village. And they are very handy, even though you need money.
All respondents: Yes.

[Why do you think the young women in this community have the same opportunities as young men in learning how to try out new farming practices?] All the two sex are free to learn about these practices. There is no one who is prevented for example from joining the group she wants to join.
But I think that most of the young women and men are not interested; business is the point. No one seems to have ever been rich from agriculture (laughter)
Worse is for us women: they make you grow crops for food to eat at home. You cannot have crops that will allow you become rich.

[We can see that maize was the leading crop grown during the past ten years and now the leading crop is rice. What has caused this change?] There are years where maize was affected much by climate in that sometimes floods destroyed farms and at other times maize did not grow due to prolonged draught.
[Was rice not affected by these climatic changes?] Rice was affected but not as maize.
All respondents: Yes.
[Why?] For example as men grow vegetables women are selling these vegetables in town or are engaged in petty business.
[Another one?] There are people who keep cattle or piggery, as other members do other farming activities, other members remain feeding the livestock.
[What could happen for example if young men tried to grow maize or rice or vegetables and sell on their own?] For the case of rice and maize, young men can grow and sell on their own.
[What challenges could they face when selling these crops?] They might face a problem of getting the market that offers good prices.

[Why is it difficult for young women to grow and sell vegetables on their own?] The selling of vegetables is commonly done by women so if a man tried to do the selling might face a difficult of getting the market as women are already used to the selling of vegetables.
[What difficulties could the young women and girls face if they tried to grow maize and rice on their own?] They could face market challenges just as men would face this challenge.
[What other challenges could they face?] All respondents are quiet.
If they own land, the household members being led by the household head will discuss about who is to do the farming where.
[What happens if at all they don’t own land?] Here each household member capable of hiring land will hire the land on his or her own.
[How do they raise the funds to hire land?] Each one can raise his or her own money or they can get the money they have been saving for farming activities.
There are some women who work on their wives plots but this is so limited in this community unless if the two are working on a common farm.
[R: Why is it rare for a man to work in her wife’s plot?] Men tend to say they are busy in economic activities like the buying and selling of crops.
This defers from one household to the other depending on how each household plans its activities.
[Between a man and a woman, who normally assists the other in plots that are individually prepared?] It is easier for a woman to work in her husband plot than a man does to her wife’s plot.
[Why do you think this is a case?] I think it is because men make themselves busy in other activities such as fishing.
All respondents: Yes.
[Which kind of labor is commonly used during agricultural activities in this community?] It is human labor commonly used and others do hire tractors.
All respondents: Yes.
[What are these responsibilities?] During farming activities sometimes we are busy with studies preparing for examinations.
[Another one?] Sometimes farming season might find us when we are caring for the sick people in the household or when we ourselves are sick.
Hiring human laborers
[Another one?] If they have money they can hire tractors.
They can invite fellow women working groups to fill this gap.
[Another one?] They can also hire more human laborers.
All respondents: Yes.

[Who.] If at all they live with the husband, they can discuss together involving other household members. If she is the only household head, she can consult the people she lives with or other close people to her.
All respondents: Yes
[Who?] The household members or his wife.
Adam will refuse her.
[Why?] Adam in his mind he thinks that Ana is aware of how the business is done and since she does not think of Ana selling and receiving the money, she will not allow her.
[Another one?] Adam will think that now Ana is going to be enlightened by working in the group. So he will not accept her to join.
Adam will automatically refuse because he has made Ana to stay at home and now he is thinking of who will do the domestic activities if Ana goes to sell the vegetable?

[Another one?] Adam will accept because he will fear that Ana’s idea to sell vegetables on her own must be out of the investigation on how the vegetables are sold so in case of refusing Adam thinks it will result into family conflicts.
All respondents: Yes.
The village members will wonder much. They will think that the wife has fed her husband with traditional medicine “limbwata” to keep him silent doing domestic activities.

[Another one with a different opinion?] In a modern way it may seem OK because the economy has changed whereby we live like white in that if a man worked in domestic activities to some people it is not a surprise but for the African traditions this is not an acceptable act for a woman to leave a man doing domestic activities. To them it will be like the world is turning around and a woman might at one day change to a man (as other respondents get into laughter)
The friends will no longer have respect for Mark because it is like he is against the tradition.
Mark will be happy of this success.

[Why?] Mark with no doubt has been thinking of whether they will make it to a better life might be Mary is messing up by deceiving me that she is selling in the market. But now once he gets to know that Mary has succeeded, Mark is now sure that life is going to be OK.
This means that both a boy and a girl have the same sex (as all respondents get into laughter).
[Another one?] This means having equal rights in everything for example if you had grown crops, it means that if you harvest and sell you have to share the income equally.
[OK. Another one?] It means that if you are doing business therefore each of the sex has the right to do business.
[Do you think gender equality is a good or a bad thing?] All respondents: Yes.
[Why?] In the past men were above all decisions but for now a man and a woman have got to discusss all the plans before them.
[Another one?] People who do things together have succeeded in life different from families where men are the final planners.
If they have a ten acres garden for example, they might get to a table and discuss that now we can sell at least eight acres and keep two acres for home consumption.
[Another one?] It is not easy for Diana to decide alone.

[Why?] In order to decide on whether to sell it means that either in the household there are needs to be fulfilled or they want to avoid perishability in the garden so each party has to present the ideas.
All respondents: Diana.

Diana will discuss with her husband and the husband will say that let me follow up to the experts to see whether this is true. They will seek advice from the agricultural extension officer and then they will try out this new farming practice.
[Do you think Diana and David will make these changes?] All respondents: Yes.

[Are there no restrictions from husbands to women who are married in as far as time is concerned?] All women move freely on their own in this village
Of course despite the fact that they have freedom to move freely in the village, they have to return home early before night. It is prohibited for a woman to return home at night.

It is not easy for them because the parents have to get convinced of the reasons as to why they are going to whatever places they are going. For example most girls here in the village go to town to work as house girls. Parents therefore have to talk to the people these girls are going to work for.
[But do they move at the end of the day?] All respondents: Yes.
They do think she had gone to practice prostitution and now she is back.
[Another one?] Other people think that she had gone to waste her time instead of staying in the village to practice the farming.
[What opportunities do they have once they return home?] Most of them return with difficult life?
[How?] You find that their life is worse than how they left. Some return when they are sick or have no clothes.
There are people who return when they are well off.
For the men it is at twenty years and for the girls seventeen to eighteen years of age.
[Do we all agree to this age?] All respondents: Yes.
This is a decision between two people a boy and a girl who want to marry each other.
[What if the two decide and the parents refute the decision?] It is not easy to refuse because the two love each other. In the past however parents used to chose for their young men who to marry.
[Is it preferable to be in a monogamous or polygamous relationship?] All respondents: Monogamous.
[What is wrong with polygamous marriage?] There are difficulties in each wife accessing the needs.

[Another one?] This was in the past when resources were still available. Land was enough but today parents have sold land so for a young man who wants to marry many men where can he get the land for all the wives to do the farming.
The right decision about marriage is that one that comes from the two people in engagement.
[Another one?] The two people a man and woman going to marry each other should pass the decision and let the community know their willingness to marry each other.

[How is the marriage process like in this community?] After a boy has agreed with the girl he is going to marry, the parents from both side are made aware, the dowry payment arrangements are made and finally the two will marry each other.
This differs in this community some have children at sixteen years while some at late twenties.

[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young men?] Education must be made a priority to all.
Young women must be provided with loans to enable them operate business.
[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young women?] Young women should be encouraged to gain more skills in entrepreneurship activities.
